subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — threat model + risk assessment internal review/sign-off
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — threat model + risk assessment internal review/sign-off

Marcus — attaching the current threat model + risk assessment for the SIEM-ready audit export beta. Looking for Security Eng sign-off (or requested changes) by end of week so we can lock the beta definition.

Key decisions captured:
- Export destinations: Splunk HEC, Datadog logs intake, S3 (customer-managed)
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once; duplicates possible; dedupe guidance required
- Scope: control-plane config + worker delivery pipeline + sink connectors + filtering

Specific questions we’d like your take on:
1) Are we comfortable with “customer-managed endpoint” risk framing (misconfig leading to exfil), with mitigations as described (RBAC, validation, audit trails, optional pause)?
2) Any additional requirements around credential storage/rotation or KMS usage?
3) Any must-have constraints for beta enablement (tenant allowlist, rate limits, etc.)?

Attachments:
- beta-siem-export-risk-assessment_v0.6.pdf
- audit-export-threat-model_v0.4.docx
- audit-event-schema-v1-draft.json

Thanks,
Naomi
Product, Security & Compliance

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:06 AM
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — threat model + risk assessment internal review/sign-off

Thanks. I skimmed and overall direction is fine, but I want a few changes before I’ll sign.

Top items:

A) Make the “customer-managed endpoint” risk more explicit in the RA and tie it to concrete controls.
- Today it reads like a generic “misconfig might leak logs.” For audit events (incl. admin actions, IPs) that’s meaningful.
- I want: clear statement that Redwood cannot validate customer ownership of endpoint; customer is responsible for securing sink.

B) Tighten mitigations around destination validation + least-privilege.
- For Splunk/Datadog: require TLS, reject plain HTTP.
- For S3: enforce SSE (SSE-S3 acceptable, SSE-KMS recommended) + guidance on bucket policy.
- Ensure we validate “host” and scheme; do not allow file:// or local addresses. In Hosted, block RFC1918 + localhost targets.

C) Credential handling requirements need to be concrete.
- Secrets must be stored in secrets manager (not DB), encrypted at rest with our KMS.
- Add requirement: rotation does not require destination recreation; editing token/key should be separate permissioned action, and it should generate an audit event.

D) Add an explicit “pause destination” control + circuit breaker.
- Threat model mentions retry storms; I want that elevated to a mitigation: auto-degrade and/or operator pause per destination to stop egress.

E) Add “audit trail of export config changes” as a must-have control for beta.
- Who created/updated/deleted destination, filter changes, credential update, paused/resumed.

Kevin/Hanae: can you take a pass and incorporate edits? I’m happy to review an updated version end of week.

Marcus
Security Engineering Lead

From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 2:34 PM
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — threat model + risk assessment internal review/sign-off

Ack. I’ll update RA + threat model this afternoon/tomorrow.

Quick clarifications/questions as I apply changes:

1) “Block RFC1918/localhost targets” — I assume this is for Hosted and Dedicated where exporter is running in our infra. For Private deployments this would break legitimate in-cluster sinks (e.g., customer runs Splunk forwarder internally). Proposed wording:
- Hosted/Dedicated: prevent private/loopback destinations (SSRF-esque / misrouting risk)
- Private: allow, but document customer responsibility and recommend network policies

2) TLS enforcement: we’ll enforce https:// for Splunk HEC and Datadog, and require cert validation (no insecure skip).

3) S3 encryption: can we make SSE-S3 mandatory and SSE-KMS “recommended” for beta? Some customers may not have KMS fully plumbed in day 1.

4) “Credential edit is separate permissioned action”: do we want separate RBAC scope beyond “manage destinations,” or is it sufficient to log and require elevated role? (We can scope it if Console team supports.)

I’ll propose concrete language + requirements and share v0.7.

Kevin
Security Engineering (SIEM export)

From: Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — threat model + risk assessment internal review/sign-off

On credential storage/rotation:

- +1 to “secrets manager only.” In Hosted/Dedicated we should specify we store destination secrets in Redwood Secrets (backed by KMS envelope encryption). No plaintext in logs.

- Rotation requirements:
  * Separate endpoint to update credentials (vs recreating destination) is helpful operationally.
  * In RA, also call out that we never display full secret values after creation; only last4 / created_at. (Console can show “token updated” but not retrieve it.)

- RBAC:
  * I recommend splitting permissions:
    - audit_export:write (create/update/delete destinations + filters)
    - audit_export:credentials_write (set/rotate token/API key)
    - audit_export:read (view destinations/health)
  * Even if product doesn’t want granular roles for beta, RA should at least require “only Admin/Owner can set credentials.”

Also recommend we add a control for secret validation without long-term retention:
- “Test delivery” should be explicit about what event is sent (test event type) and should not leak actual audit events during setup.

Hanae
Security Engineering (Secrets & Credentials)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — threat model + risk assessment internal review/sign-off

Adding SRE POV on the retry storm / egress safety portion.

I’d like the RA to explicitly include:
- Per-destination circuit breaker (e.g., if sustained 5xx/429 beyond threshold -> destination transitions to DEGRADED and stops sending for cooldown)
- Manual pause/resume (customer-initiated) AND operator pause (SRE-initiated) that is auditable
- Backpressure/rate limits: exporter must not impact primary API latency. This should be listed as a reliability + security mitigation (avoid cascading failures)

I’m attaching the checklist snippet we’ve been using for launch readiness — feel free to cite it.

Attachment:
- SRE-launch-readiness-checklist_audit-export_beta.txt

Sean
SRE Lead

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 9:27 AM
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — threat model + risk assessment internal review/sign-off

From GRC angle, +1 on making responsibilities explicit. Two asks for the document set:

1) Add a short “Shared Responsibility” section (customer vs Redwood) for:
- securing the destination endpoint/bucket/index
- configuring retention and access controls in their SIEM
- validating they are not exporting to an unintended third-party environment

2) Clarify data classification / PII posture:
- Audit events may include IP address, user identifiers, and admin actions.
- State redaction rules (e.g., no prompt content; no API payloads; no secrets).

3) Evidence alignment:
- Call out that we log changes to export config (this helps SOC 2 CC6/CC7 evidence).
- Mention encryption in transit and at rest for secrets and buffering.

No blockers beyond what Marcus listed.

Olga
GRC / Compliance

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 21, 2025 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — threat model + risk assessment internal review/sign-off

Reviewed the updated v0.7 (Kevin shared via Drive) and the edits look good. Specifically:
- Shared responsibility section added with clear customer vs Redwood boundaries
- Hosted/Dedicated: destination validation blocks private/loopback; Private deployments noted as customer-controlled networking
- TLS enforcement is explicit (no HTTP, no cert bypass)
- Secrets manager + KMS is explicit; “no secret retrieval” in Console is stated
- Export config changes are explicitly audited (create/update/delete destination; filter change; credentials rotation; pause/resume)
- Circuit breaker / pause controls are listed as required mitigations

Security Eng sign-off from my side for beta, contingent on the implementation matching the stated controls (ENG-13933 + ENG-13932 + RBAC/audit trail PR).

Naomi: you can treat this as approval to proceed to beta enablement planning.

Marcus
Security Engineering Lead
